sentences.text:
The short facts are these:
It is stated that petitioners 1 to 3 are the owners and possessors of the land bearing Sy.No.78 measuring 11 Acres 15 Guntas and it is their ancestral property, that was earlier standing in the name of Ashamma W/o.Kashappa.

After demise of Ashamma,
the said land was mutated in the name of petitioners 1 to 3 and till today the name of the petitioners 1 and 2 is entered in the ROR of Sy.No.78.

It is stated that petitioners 4 and 5 are the owners and possessors of the land bearing Sy.No.118/5 measuring 5 Acres 29 Guntas, that was earlier standing in the name of Bheemamma W/o.Narasappa and after her demise, the said land was mutated in the name of petitioners 4 and 5.

The petitioners being the absolute owners and possessors of the said lands, due to draught in the village, went to Maharashtra for coolie work and continued their coolie work there and they never visited the lands for several years.

They returned to the NC: 2025:KHC-K:5226 HC-KAR Village somewhere during 2025 and they came to know that respondents without having any right, title and interest over the said land have taken up construction of Government Hospital, School, Library, Samudaya Bhavan and Water Tank, etc.
The petitioners contend that the said construction is illegal without initiating acquisition proceedings and without payment of compensation.

Accordingly, they made representations before the respondent authorities on 04.12.2024 vide Annexures-D, E, F and G thereby, requesting that they being the absolute owners of the said lands and the Government is illegally started construction over the same without initiating acquisition proceedings and without payment of compensation and requested to pay the compensation accordingly for the acquired land.
Aggrieved by the inaction on the part of the respondents, the petitioners are before this Court.
4. Counsel for the respective parties urged several contentions.

Sri.Manjunath Ginni., counsel for the petitioners submits that the inaction on the part of the respondents in not considering the representations at Annexures-D, E, F and G and not paying the compensation is bad in law.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:5226 HC-KAR

Next, he submits that the respondents are bound to consider the representations submitted by petitioners at Annexures-D, E, F and G and initiate acquisition proceedings and pay compensation as per the Right to Fair Compensation Act, 2013.

A further submission is made that as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in VIDYADEVI's case, the State is bound to initiate acquisition proceedings and pay compensation, without acquisition and payment of compensation, respondents have no right to put-up constructions illegally.
Therefore, the act of respondents is bad in law.
Lastly, he submitted that appropriate Writ may be issued directing the respondents to consider the representations submitted by the petitioner.

sentences.text: Urging several contentions, AGA submits that an appropriate order may be passed.

5. Heard the arguments and perused the Writ papers with care.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:5226 HC-KAR 6.
The Writ Petition is filed seeking a suitable direction in the form of Mandamus to compel the Public Authority to discharge their statutory obligations.

Mandamus is a judicial remedy issued in the form of an order from the Supreme Court or a High Court to any constitutional, statutory or a non-statutory agency - to do or to forbear from doing some specific act which that agency is obliged to do or refrain from doing under the law and which is in the nature of a public duty or a statutory duty.
It is considered as a residuary remedy of public law.
It is a general remedy whenever justice has been declined to any person.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the Government has taken away their lands to construct Government Hospital, School, Library, Samudaya Bhavan and Water Tank etc., in their lands without prior notice or any kind of information to the petitioners.
Hence, they made several representations.
One representation is dated 04.12.2024 and the same is at Annexure-D.

Other three representations are dated 04.12.2024 and the same are at Annexures-E, F and G. NC:
2025:KHC-K:5226 HC-KAR I have perused the same with utmost care.
They are representations submitted by the petitioners.
The respondents have not considered the representations of petitioners till date though the same needed immediate attention.
The petitioners have able to show the specific demand for the fulfillment of a duty and there is a specific inaction of the performance of a duty.

In so far as the present petition is concerned, the respondents are hereby directed to consider the representations of the petitioners at Annexure-D, E, F and G and dispose of the same by giving suitable reasons in accordance with the law within three months from the receipt of the certified copy of this order.
This Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of case.
7. Resultantly, the Writ Petition is allowed.
